quoted_tweet.text:
Here's your 10-step guide to mastering Claude Code:

1. Stop Working in Chat Windows 

Traditional chat interfaces force you to manually copy-paste files one at a time. Claude Code lives in your terminal and automatically reads entire folder structures. Open terminal in your project folder, type claude, and it instantly has context of all your files.

2. Build Your Knowledge Base First 

Create a four-folder structure before you start: https://t.co/gFaUVTeDNX (your product, market, strategy), writing-styles/ (internal, technical, user-friendly voices), examples/ (past PRDs, analyses, reports), and meeting-transcripts/ (auto-uploaded recordings).

3. Use the CLAUDE File 

The CLAUDE file (all caps) is your project's permanent memory system. Add rules once and they persist across every session forever: "Never commit without asking first," "Always use technical writing style," "Format research as bullet points."

4. Save Your Best Prompts 

Create commands like /meeting-notes, /competitive-research, or /prd-review. Save your most-used prompts once, then execute them instantly by typing the command. No more searching through Twitter bookmarks or Google Docs for that prompt you saved 3 months ago.

5. Use Plan Mode First 

Press Shift+Tab before complex tasks. Claude creates a plan without executing. Review, catch mistakes, then approve. This prevents 80% of disasters and saves hours of debugging.

6. Run Parallel Agents 

Multiple similar tasks? Spin up parallel agents. Three customer interviews = three UXR agents working simultaneously. A week of work becomes one hour through true parallelization.

7. Build Specialized Agents 

Create custom agents with different perspectives: Designer agent (UX focused), Engineer agent (technical constraints), Executive agent (business impact). All three can review your PRD simultaneously, each providing specialized feedback from their unique viewpoint.

8. Use the $37 Stack 

You don't need the $200 Claude Max plan. Claude Pro costs $17/month and handles all research, writing, and document work perfectly with the Sonnet model. Add Cursor for $20/month when you need heavy coding with better models like Opus. Total: $37/month.

9. Monitor Token Usage 

Claude Code shows real-time token costs. Finally understand "$1.50 per million tokens." Use visibility to manage context—clear sessions after tasks, use Plan Mode before expensive runs.

10. Scale Week by Week 

Week 1: One research task with auto file-reading. 
Week 2: Add https://t.co/gFaUVTeDNX. 
Week 3: First custom command. 
Week 4: Try parallel agents. 
Week 5: Build custom agent. Each week adds one capability.

tweets.text:
Best practices for Claude Code

- Verify Outputs Early: Always give Claude verification tools like tests, screenshots, or expected results to catch errors - think self-checking AI for reliable code.
- Workflow: Explore > Plan > Code > Commit: Use Plan Mode to research first, then outline steps before implementing; skip for tiny fixes to avoid wrong turns.
- Prompt Precisely: Include file refs, constraints, and codebase patterns in prompts - vague ones for exploration, specific for execution.
- Enrich Prompts with Content: @-mention files, paste images/URLs, or let Claude fetch data to boost context without overload.
- Setup CLAUDE md & Environment: Create a persistent config file with commands, styles, and rules; add permissions, tools, subagents for scalable workflows.
- Communicate Like a Teammate: Ask codebase Qs or let Claude "interview" you for specs - treat it as a senior dev collab.
- Session Management Hacks: Use /rewind, subagents, or clear contexts to prevent bloat; checkpoints for easy resets.
- Scale with Automation: Run headless, parallel sessions, or fan-out tasks - perfect for CI or batch ops in sandboxes.
- Dodge Pitfalls: Avoid mega-sessions, over-corrections, or blind trust - scope tight and prune configs.
- Build Intuition: Experiment, reflect on interactions to master prompting.
